{"items": ["[passage_read_so_far]
- Poole comes to Utterson's house at night and says something is wrong.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole says the doctor has shut himself in the cabinet and he is afraid.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole says he thinks there has been foul play.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Utterson rises, takes hat and greatcoat, and follows Poole.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- They walk through the cold deserted London streets to the house.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- They enter the hall where all the servants are huddled in fear.（Mr. Utterson、Poole、the housemaid、the cook）
- The housemaid whimpers and the maid weeps loudly.（Mr. Utterson、Poole、the housemaid）
- Poole orders the knife-boy to bring a candle.（Poole、the knife-boy）
- Poole leads Utterson to the laboratory and tells him to listen quietly.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole knocks and calls that Utterson asks to see him.（Poole、the voice）
- The voice inside complains that it cannot see anyone.（the voice）
- Poole asks whether that was his master's voice; Utterson says it seems much changed.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole declares his master was made away with eight days ago.（Poole）
- Utterson calls the tale wild and argues a murderer would not stay.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole tells of a week of notes demanding a pure drug from chemists.（Poole）
- Poole hands Utterson a crumpled note from Dr. Jekyll to Messrs. Maw.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Utterson notes the handwriting is the doctor's; Poole says he has seen him.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole tells Utterson he saw a masked figure in the cabinet.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson suggests Jekyll suffers a deforming disease and hides his face.（Mr. Utterson）
- Poole insists the masked thing was not Jekyll but a dwarf.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson resolves to break in the cabinet door.（Mr. Utterson）
- Poole and Utterson agree to break in together.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Poole fetches an axe and suggests Utterson take the kitchen poker.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson warns Poole they are placing themselves in peril.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Poole says the masked figure was Mr. Hyde.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson says he once spoke with Hyde.（Mr. Utterson）
- Poole describes Hyde as giving a cold, thin feeling.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson summons Bradshaw and orders him to guard the laboratory door.（Mr. Utterson、Bradshaw）
- Poole and Utterson wait in the theatre and hear pacing footsteps.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Poole says the walker weeps like a woman or lost soul.（Poole、Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson demands to see Jekyll and threatens brute force.（Mr. Utterson）
- The voice begs Utterson for mercy.（Mr. Utterson、the voice）
- Utterson recognizes the voice as Hyde's and orders the door down.（Mr. Utterson）
- Poole strikes the door five times with the axe until it bursts.（Poole）
- They peer in and find the contorted body of Edward Hyde.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Utterson concludes Hyde is a self-destroyer by the crushed phial.（Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson says they must now find Jekyll's body.（Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson and Poole search the theatre, cabinet, closets and cellar for Jekyll.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- They find the by-street door locked with a rusty broken key lying nearby.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- They examine the cabinet and find chemical apparatus and white salt on saucers.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- They find a pious book annotated by Jekyll with startling blasphemies.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- They look into the cheval-glass and see only the room and their own pale faces.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Utterson opens an envelope addressed to him and finds a will naming himself instead of Hyde.（Mr. Utterson）
- Utterson reads Jekyll's dated note and concludes Jekyll was alive that day and may have fled.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Poole hands Utterson a sealed packet, the third enclosure.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
- Utterson decides to go home, read the documents, and return before midnight to send for the police.（Mr. Utterson、Poole）
